name: Alufluoride Ltd
tagline: Niche import-substitution moat (Aluminium Fluoride) with a real expansion (24,000 TPA, completed Aug 2026) - but Q1 FY27 revenue fell ~40% YoY because primary feedstock supplier Coromandel has chronically under-delivered its contracted FSA quantity 'since inception', a structural supply risk the market hadn't fully seen until this print
business_overview: Alufluoride manufactures Aluminium Fluoride (AlF3), a critical flux for aluminium smelters, using a low-cost 'waste-to-wealth' process (Hydrofluosilicic Acid, a fertilizer-industry byproduct) licensed from Alusuisse, Switzerland -- one of only two Indian AlF3 producers using this cheaper route versus fluorspar-based/imported alternatives.
fundamentals_table: Net cash (net D/E -0.10); debt-averse with strong cash flows
9M FY26 revenue Rs 156.18 Cr vs Rs 131.89 Cr 9M FY25 (+18.4%); FY26 net profit +55.9% YoY; but Q4 FY26 saw margin compression despite revenue resilience
fundamentals_narrative: Genuinely undemanding micro-cap with a real, specific import-substitution moat: India's total AlF3 demand is ~80,000 TPA against combined domestic production of only ~23,000 TPA (Alufluoride ~18,000 + Greenstar ~5,000), meaning most demand is still met by imports -- a real runway for domestic capacity gains. FY26 delivered a record standalone revenue of Rs 208.76 Cr (+10.7%) and PAT of Rs 24.29 Cr (+32.7%), ROCE has held a strong, stable 24-25% for 3 years, and the 24,000 TPA capacity expansion (from 18,000) completed in Aug 2026, alongside solar capacity now at 4.1 MW. But Q4 FY26 already showed margin compression, and Q1 FY27 was materially worse: revenue fell ~40% YoY (Rs 25.97 Cr vs Rs 42.93 Cr) on reduced production, because the company's primary contracted FSA (Hydrofluosilicic Acid feedstock) supplier, Coromandel International, has been unable to supply its full contracted 4,000 TPA quantity 'since inception' -- forcing costlier/uncertain balance sourcing from Odisha. This is a structural feedstock-reliability problem, not the cyclical raw-material-price issue the Jan-2026 trusted-user summary (and the planned Alumina Hydrate backward-integration project) was framed around -- and it directly undercuts the low-cost-feedstock moat the whole thesis rests on if the new 24,000 TPA capacity can't be reliably fed.
technical_read: Not checked -- fundamentals/moat specifics were the primary signal.
sentiment_summary: Read the most recent 15 of 73 posts (thread spans years, low overall activity but with one substantive recent contribution). Historical thread activity includes a mysterious ~20% price jump (Nov 2024) with no public news explaining it, and repeated retail questions about a planned Jordan JV that generated uncertainty for over a year.
community_signal: kdjolly (trusted, elevated) posted a detailed, well-sourced executive summary (Jan 2026) reframing the Jordan JV withdrawal (announced most recently, Aug 2026, per company PPT) as a deliberate de-risking move given Gaza-conflict-related Middle East instability, redirecting capital toward a domestic Alumina Hydrate backward-integration project (Rs 40-50 Cr Phase 1 capex, 30,000-50,000 TPA) intended to stabilize input costs and expand margins.

trusted_signals.note: Detailed bull thesis: ~20-25% domestic AlF3 market share, large import-substitution runway (80,000 TPA demand vs ~23,000 TPA total domestic supply), capacity expansion to 18,000 TPA, captive solar for margin protection, and a domestic Alumina Hydrate backward-integration project to fix input-cost volatility.

bse_notes: Aug 2026 investor PPT confirms Jordan JV exit is complete.
bull_case: Real, quantified import-substitution runway (80,000 TPA India demand vs ~23,000 TPA total domestic supply) in a niche, technically-licensed (Alusuisse) process with only one domestic competitor

Concrete, funded expansion plans (capacity to 18,000 TPA, captive solar for ~85% of energy needs, planned Alumina Hydrate backward integration) all aimed directly at the two things that would drive a re-rating: volume growth and margin stability
bear_case: Feedstock-supply reliability, not just price volatility, is the real near-term risk: Coromandel (the primary contracted FSA supplier, meant to supply 4,000 TPA exclusively) has chronically under-delivered 'since inception' - Q1 FY27 revenue fell ~40% YoY on reduced production as a direct result, and management's hope for recovery 'from the current quarter' is unproven
The new 24,000 TPA capacity (completed Aug 2026) is worth little if feedstock can't be secured at volume - the alternate Odisha source is a workaround, not a proven fix
The backward-integration project (Alumina Hydrate, Rs 40-50 Cr Phase 1) targets input-cost volatility, not this specific supply-volume shortfall - it may not even address the Coromandel problem
Cash conversion weakened sharply in FY26 (OCF/EBITDA-proxy ~125%->~59%; FCF near-zero) against a large Rs ~59 Cr capex year for the expansion

Very thin trading/community interest (only 73 posts over years, one unexplained ~20% price spike with no public news) means limited independent scrutiny of management's claims - the Jan-2026 bull writeup pre-dates and did not anticipate this Q1 FY27 feedstock disruption
verdict_headline: Deep-dive pass 1 finds the moat's key input is not reliably sourceable: Coromandel has chronically under-delivered contracted FSA feedstock, driving a ~40% Q1 FY27 revenue decline - conviction cut to Low-Medium pending proof the shortfall actually resolves
verdict_reasoning: The market-share/demand math (80,000 TPA India demand vs ~23,000 TPA domestic supply) is still real and intact - the import-substitution TAM/tailwind case is unaffected by this pass

But the moat depends on a specific, cheap byproduct feedstock (FSA) being reliably available, and the primary contracted supplier (Coromandel) has chronically under-delivered 'since inception' - not a one-quarter blip. This is new information the Jan-2026 trusted-user writeup did not have visibility into, and it directly caused the Q1 FY27 ~40% revenue decline

four_box moat downgraded yes->weak (feedstock reliability undercuts the theoretical cost advantage); score 3.5->3.0, still clearing the >=3.0 threshold so thesis_fit 10x-in-2-3-years is retained, but conviction is set independently

Conviction cut Medium -> Low-Medium: strong balance sheet (net cash, ROCE 24-25% for 3 years) and real TAM, but a currently-unresolved, structurally-described supply bottleneck on the exact input the whole cost-advantage thesis rests on is a real, not cosmetic, risk. Revisit once a post-Q1-FY27 quarter confirms whether the Coromandel/Odisha feedstock situation has actually normalised

four_box.note: Import-substitution runway (80,000 TPA India demand vs ~23,000 TPA domestic supply) and capacity expansion still support tailwind/tam; moat downgraded to weak this pass - the Alusuisse-licensed low-cost process only works if the FSA feedstock is actually available, and primary supplier Coromandel has chronically under-delivered its contracted quantity since inception, driving a ~40% Q1 FY27 revenue decline. Valuation stays weak - 15.8x P/E with an unresolved supply risk is not obviously cheap.

Root cause found: Coromandel International Ltd was contracted to supply 4,000 TPA of Hydrofluosilicic Acid (FSA) exclusively to Alufluoride from its new Kakinada plant, but 'has been unable to supply the contracted quantity since inception' - the balance is being sourced from Odisha

deep_dive.conviction_update: Medium -> Low-Medium. The TAM/tailwind case is intact, but this pass uncovered that the moat's core input (cheap FSA feedstock) has a chronic, since-inception reliability problem with the primary contracted supplier, which just caused a ~40% quarterly revenue decline. That is a materially different and more serious risk than the 'margin compression from raw-material price volatility' framing in the existing write-up, and it remains unresolved as of the latest data found.
